meteogal2fdata

meteogal2fdata downloads daily observations from the MeteoGalicia meteorological-station network, preserves the validation code associated with each measurement, and converts the resulting daily data to functional data objects (fdata and ldata) from fda.usc.

The package deliberately keeps the workflow simple: base R data.frame objects are the intermediate representation, measurements are not imputed, and quality filtering is separated from downloading so that the same raw files can be reused with different validation criteria.

Interactive app: meteogal2shiny (station map, download, validation codes and functional data, no installation needed) · Website: https://moviedo5.github.io/meteogal2fdata/

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("moviedo5/meteogal2fdata", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Data source: MeteoGalicia, Xunta de Galicia. Data may be reused according to the MeteoGalicia legal notice, with MeteoGalicia cited as the source.

Main functions

Function Purpose
meteogal2inventory() Obtain station metadata or reconstruct an inventory from local data
meteogal2download() Resumable station-year downloads with raw values, validation codes and provenance
meteogal2df() Read daily observations as a base R data.frame and choose the validation criterion
meteogal2fdata() Convert one variable to one 365-day functional curve per station-year
meteogal2lfdata() Convert several variables to an aligned ldata object
meteogal_qc_codes() Describe the MeteoGalicia validation codes used by the package

Validation codes

Each measurement can be accompanied by lnCodigoValidacion. The package keeps that code in qc_<variable> and uses English descriptions consistently:

code description default quality = c(1, 5)
0 Not validated excluded
1 Valid original used
2 Suspect excluded
3 Erroneous always missing
5 Valid interpolated used
9 Not recorded always missing 
library(meteogal2fdata)
meteogal_qc_codes()

Downloads are not filtered. Quality is selected when the files are read:

x <- meteogal2df(data_dir = "meteogal_daily")
# default: quality = c(1, 5)

x_recent <- meteogal2df(
  data_dir = "meteogal_daily",
  quality = c(0, 1, 5)
)

Values rejected by quality become NA, but their qc_ codes remain available. Codes 3 and 9 and the sentinel value -9999 are always treated as missing. The package does not otherwise impute or interpolate missing values.

Downloading daily observations

The following example compares two stations with a clearer climatic contrast: Coruña-Torre de Hércules (10157) and Ourense (10148).

log <- meteogal2download(
  start_date = "2023-01-01",
  end_date = "2024-12-31",
  station_ids = c("10157", "10148"),
  vars = c("temp_mean", "temp_min", "temp_max", "prec"),
  format = "csv",
  out_dir = "meteogal_daily"
)

Files are written by station and year. The file meteogal_daily/_meteogal_manifest.csv records their provenance. RDS files also store provenance in attr(x, "meteogal_meta") and units in attr(x, "units").

Functional data

meteogal2fdata() creates one 365-day curve per station-year for one variable:

fd <- meteogal2fdata(
  file = "meteogal_daily",
  station_id = c("10157", "10148"),
  var = "temp_mean"
)
plot(fd)

meteogal2lfdata() creates aligned functional variables plus station-year metadata:

inv <- meteogal2inventory()
ld <- meteogal2lfdata(
  file = "meteogal_daily",
  station_ids = c("10157", "10148"),
  vars = c("temp_mean", "temp_min", "temp_max", "prec"),
  inventory = inv
)

ld$df[, c("station_id", "station_name", "year", "altitude", "lon", "lat",
          "n_temp_mean_valid")]
plot(ld$temp_mean)

February 29 is removed from leap years so that March 1 is always day 60. Missing measurements remain NA. The daily validation-code matrices qc_<variable> and the original date matrix fecha are retained in ldata$df and remain aligned when the object is subset.

Spatial exploration

meteogal2inventory() returns longitude, latitude and altitude as ordinary numeric columns, so simple maps require no additional spatial package. The spatial vignette illustrates:

  • the station network coloured by altitude;
  • annual mean daily temperature by station, using the selected validation criterion and reporting the number of usable days.

The temperature map is a station-level descriptive map, not an interpolated surface.

Real reproducible examples

Run:

source("data-raw/build-example.R")

to generate the bundled real-data examples from MeteoGalicia. The script creates:

  • meteogal_example.csv: Coruña-Torre de Hércules and Ourense, 2023-2024;
  • meteogal_example_inventory.rds: metadata for those stations;
  • meteogal_inventory.csv: current station inventory;
  • meteogal_temperature_2024.csv: annual mean temperature for the spatial example.

No observations in these files are simulated.

Vignettes

  • daily-data-and-quality: download, CSV/RDS files, validation codes, provenance and missing values.
  • spatial-stations: station inventory, altitude map and temperature map.
  • functional-data: conversion to fdata/ldata and integration with fda.usc.
  • meteogalicia-es: complete workflow in Spanish, from download and maps to functional data.

Shiny application

The application is online at https://manueloviedo.shinyapps.io/meteogal2shiny/.

The interactive application meteogal2shiny (station map, download, validation codes and functional data) is kept in a separate folder, meteogal2fdata_shiny/, with the same structure as aemet2shiny and omie2shiny, so that this package keeps only base R, jsonlite and fda.usc as dependencies. See its README.md to run it locally or deploy it to shinyapps.io.
